methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Richmond's young workforce facing AI pressure signals shallow, platform-driven adoption where workers must adapt to AI tools without necessarily building deep technical capability—classic 'software does it for you' dynamics in a secondary metro hub.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents potential distributed capacity building, though success depends on whether programs develop deep AI fluency or just surface-level platform skills in an economically transitioning region.

signals.title: Norfolk Southern deploys AI system to catch wheel defects before they break - The Business Journals
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Southern deploying sophisticated AI defect detection systems demonstrates deep technical implementation in Hampton Roads' industrial base, but represents enterprise-led concentration rather than distributed workforce capability development.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon expanding Scale AI contract to $500M and TurbineOne relocating HQ to NoVA crystallizes defense-AI concentration in the region, deepening the capability gap as federal dollars and specialized talent cluster in the metro corridor.

signals.title: Data or Water? Safety or Privacy? Roanoke Faces Tradeoffs as New Technology and Legislation Reshape Daily Life - The Roanoke Rambler
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke grappling with data/water tradeoffs and technology governance questions without clear pathways to AI capability development signals communities facing AI's infrastructure demands while missing opportunities for meaningful participation in the AI economy.
